summary: Sync between Redwood and CloudPeak to align on marketplace listing and joint reference architecture. Discussed required assets for listing, high-level network and security patterns for the reference deployment, KMS/SSO requirements, and pilot scope/timeline. Agreed next steps to exchange diagrams, security docs, and provision a demo sandbox.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex and Priya from Redwood.
[00:08] Sam Chen (CloudPeak PM): Sam here, Liu and Rachel on the line too.
[00:12] Liu Zhao (CloudPeak CTO): Hi all.
[00:14] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Great. I put a short agenda — marketplace listing steps, reference arch, security integration, and pilot timeline.
[00:22] Sam Chen: Works for us. We mainly want to understand what we need for the Marketplace listing and how the reference architecture will look when we bake Redwood into our platform.
[00:30] Alex Martinez: Cool. High level — marketplace listing is a few buckets: marketing assets, technical listing metadata, and a validated reference architecture + integration guide. We'll also need a manifest for billing and SKUs if you want us to surface it in the CloudPeak marketplace.
[00:44] Rachel Turner (CloudPeak Sec): On security, we'll need SOC 2 evidence, SSO/SAML flow, and KMS integration details. Also data residency questions.
[00:52] Priya Singh: Totally. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via our K M S integration — sometimes the transcriber writes that as K V cash, sorry about that — you can use either cloud KMS or an HSM through our private deployment.
[01:06] Liu Zhao: For the reference arch, can you show the VPC peering option vs private deployment? We have strict egress rules so VPC is preferred.
[01:16] Priya Singh: Sure. At a high level: hosted (our cloud) -> simple integration but data egress; dedicated -> reserved capacity in our infra with isolation; private -> we run a control plane but you host inference in your V P C or on-prem. For VPC peering you'd see an architecture where requests route through a private endpoint, KV cache lives local to the cluster, and control plane communicates over a management channel.
[01:36] Sam Chen: When you say KV cache, is that client side or inside Redwood?
[01:40] Priya Singh: It's inside the inference layer — key value cache for autoregressive workloads. Helps with prefix caching to save token costs.
[01:46] Alex Martinez: A note on marketplace listing: Cloud marketplaces often require a packaged listing with screenshots, a 1 pager, logo assets, and a short technical description. We can share an example listing from another partner.
[01:58] Sam Chen: Perfect. On pricing — do you have a standard model we should reference for the listing? Per-token billing or reserved capacity pricing?
[02:06] Alex Martinez: Both. For hosted we'll surface per-token/embedding rates; for Dedicated it's typically an hourly or monthly reserved capacity SKU. For marketplace it's common to list both and funnel enterprise leads to a reserved contract.
[02:18] Rachel Turner: For SAML, we will want SCIM for user provisioning too. Any gap there?
[02:26] Priya Singh: We support SAML SSO and can integrate SCIM for provisioning on the private deployment and dedicated. Hosted supports SSO for console access; provisioning flows differ slightly. We'll include the integration matrix in the doc.
[02:37] Liu Zhao: How about auditing and logs? Our compliance team will want each request traceable back to an org user.
[02:44] Priya Singh: We emit audit logs — per-request traces, token-level cost, model used, route, latency. You can forward logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud log sinks depending on deployment.
[02:54] Sam Chen: Great. Are there known blockers to listing on CloudPeak marketplace VS AWS/GCP?
[03:00] Alex Martinez: Not really blockers; each marketplace has specific asset and security requirements. CloudPeak's onboarding is fairly straightforward but they'll want a validated reference deployment and a security questionnaire filled. We'll help with both.
[03:12] Sam Chen: Sweet. Let's dig into the reference architecture details — can you talk through network flow for the VPC peering pattern?
[03:20] Priya Singh: Yeah. Slide — imagine CloudPeak VPC peering to Redwood inference VPC or using PrivateLink equivalent. Traffic enters a private endpoint, NATing is minimized, KV cache and batching reside on the inference nodes in your region. If you have strict egress policies we can co-host the inference nodes in your cloud region or run an on-prem variant.
[03:42] Liu Zhao: Co-hosted inference nodes — that is the private deployment?
[03:45] Priya Singh: Exactly. Private deployment is where you host runtime, we provide control plane connectivity optionally. It satisfies data residency, KMS control, and tighter network controls.
[03:55] Rachel Turner: For KMS, do you support customer key rotation and bring-your-own-key?
[03:59] Priya Singh: Yes — BYOK and rotation are supported. We'll include key lifecycle docs.
[04:04] Sam Chen: On the implementation timeline — if we start a pilot, how long to have a validated listing and reference arch?
[04:11] Alex Martinez: Typical pilot is 4–6 weeks to validate performance and integration. Marketplace listing can go live in parallel; initial draft listing within 1–2 weeks, final assets and security review next 2–3 weeks.
[04:23] Sam Chen: Good. Who else should be involved from our side?
[04:26] Liu Zhao: I'll pull in infra and networking, Rachel will lead security, and we'll have a product owner to drive requirements.
[04:32] Alex Martinez: Awesome. A couple of product notes: for cost control we recommend enabling prefix/K V cache and adaptive batching. Also, when we recommend quantization profiles for certain models, that'll go into the reference arch as a recommended path.
[04:47] Sam Chen: Can you share an example of how quantization affects latency and accuracy tradeoffs?
[04:53] Priya Singh: Yep — we'll include results from internal benchmarks: int8 reduces memory and can slightly increase latency throughput while small perf hit to quality on some models; we document per-model recommendations. Expect a short table in the reference doc (we'll attach).
[05:04] Rachel Turner: About the billing integration — for marketplace, do we need to map SKUs?
[05:08] Alex Martinez: Yes, create SKUs for reserved capacity and for API credits. We'll provide naming conventions and mappings. For CloudPeak's marketplace APIs, we can plug into their metering as well.
[05:17] Sam Chen: Any red flags we should be aware of around egress/data handling?
[05:21] Priya Singh: If you use hosted mode, ensure customers accept egress to Redwood regions. For private/dedicated, egress is controlled. We'll document the tradeoffs in the guide.
[05:31] Liu Zhao: On the integration work — who owns the reference deployment demo environment?
[05:35] Alex Martinez: Redwood can spin up the Redwood side of the demo and we ask CloudPeak to provide a VPC/test account for peering. We can also run a fully private demo in your environment if needed.
[05:45] Sam Chen: Ok. Let's capture concrete deliverables.
[05:48] Alex Martinez: I'll list them in the meeting notes: reference architecture diagram, marketplace listing draft, security questionnaire answers, demo tenant setup, pricing SKUs.
[05:57] Priya Singh: I'll start the reference diagram and sample deployment templates — Terraform snippets maybe — and share by next Tuesday.
[06:05] Rachel Turner: We'll get SOC2 cert and the security contacts over. One question — do you support customer-managed logging sinks?
[06:13] Priya Singh: Yes, you can configure log export to your cloud logging. We'll include example log config.
[06:19] Sam Chen: Sounds good. A few clarifying Qs — what parts of the reference arch would we need to vet for compliance?
[06:26] Rachel Turner: Network flows, key management, log retention and access controls. Also how the control plane communicates with our environment.
[06:33] Priya Singh: All valid — we'll add a compliance checklist in the doc.
[06:36] Sam Chen: Great. Any other questions from CloudPeak?
[06:39] Liu Zhao: One small thing — how do model updates and rollouts happen in private? We need predictable maintenance windows and canary control.
[06:46] Priya Singh: We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous model variants. For private deployments we can schedule maintenance windows and disable auto-rollouts if you want stricter control.
[06:58] Alex Martinez: Ok, looks like we're aligned. Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:03] Alex Martinez: Recap — Redwood to share reference arch and marketplace draft; CloudPeak to provide security docs and test accounts; both to provision demo tenant and schedule security deep dive.
[07:14] Sam Chen: Confirmed. I'll write up pilot scope and success metrics and send by Friday.
[07:19] Rachel Turner: I'll share SOC2 and contact.
[07:22] Liu Zhao: I'll loop infra.
[07:24] Priya Singh: I'll post the architecture diagram and Terraform snippets by 2025-10-21.
[07:29] Alex Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the notes and links.
[07:33] Sam Chen: Thanks all.
[07:35] (meeting ends)
